items.title: What evidence can you prepare before applying for a delivery position?

values: Material setup｜all editorially fictional
R1 route stop order: stop 1 at 10 Pine Street, stop 2 at 12 Pine Street, stop 3 at 5 River Road. All three addresses and mail numbers are entirely fictional and do not correspond to real deliveries.

A1 is an ordinary letter addressed to 12 Pine Street; under the exercise rules, the address matches and the mailbox is usable, so stop 2 may be recorded as delivered. A2 is a registered parcel addressed to 5 River Road that must be signed for by the recipient, but the recipient is absent.
A3 is a parcel addressed to 18 Pine Street; that address is not on the R1 list. The exercise is paper-based only and does not touch real mail or customer data.
Task and deliverable｜45 minutes

0–5 minutes read the R1 and the three item conditions; 5–20 minutes write a three-row table listing item number, address, stop, signature condition, status, basis and next step; 20–30 minutes write the A2/A3 handover; 30–40 minutes review independently; 40–45 minutes score against the rubric below and revise.

The handover sheet lists the item number, known facts, prohibited actions, information pending verification and next responsible person separately. The paper exercise time is recorded as T0; the next responsible person is uniformly the fictional R1 station supervisor, and no route or signature may be added on one's own.
Reference answer and handover example

A1｜12 Pine Street｜stop 2｜ordinary letter, mailbox usable｜recorded as delivered in the exercise｜address matches｜log exercise complete. A2｜5 River Road｜stop 3｜requires recipient signature but recipient absent｜delivery attempt／pending｜signature not satisfied｜return-to-station handover. A3｜18 Pine Street｜stop unknown｜delivery conditions still to be checked｜route pending verification｜R1 has no such address｜pause delivery and refer to the station supervisor.

T0 handover of A2: recipient absent, no signature obtained; recording as delivered or signing on the recipient's behalf is prohibited; institutional notification and follow-up process pending verification, referred to the R1 station supervisor for confirmation. T0 handover of A3: address not on the list; guessing the stop or altering the address is prohibited; route ownership and arrangement pending verification, referred to the same supervisor for confirmation.

Recalculated status: 1 item completed (A1), 2 items pending (A2/A3), 3 items in total; the unknown route of A3 does not equal stop 4. This status is only a deduction from the fictional task and is not a real scan record that has occurred.
Review rubric｜editorial self-assessment, not an employer examination

Four items scored 0–2 each, total 0–8: (a) stops: 2 points if A1 stop 2, A2 stop 3 and A3 unknown are all correct, 1 point if only partly correct, 0 points for guessing the A3 stop; (b) status: 2 points if A1 recorded as delivered in the exercise, A2 as attempt pending and A3 as pending verification, with 1+2=3 correct, 1 point if one status or the count is missing, 0 points for falsely recording A2 as delivered.

(c) handover: 2 points if A2/A3 each have all five items complete — facts, prohibited actions, pending verification and supervisor, and T0 — 1 point if an item is missing, 0 points for no handover or for altering the route or signing on someone's behalf; (d) boundaries: 2 points for clearly stating it is fictional, using no real data and following institutional rules afterwards, 1 point if one item is missed, 0 points for using real customer data or claiming official delivery procedures.

Error example: marking A2 as delivered, guessing A3 as stop 4, writing no handover but stating that it is fictional. Four items scored 0／0／0／2, total 2/8; first restore A2 as pending, A3 as unknown and 1 completed +2 pending, then add the T0 supervisor handover. The score only helps revise the work sample and does not prove a driving licence, postal authorization or hiring.

subject.summary: Postal service mail carriers deliver and collect mail on established routes on foot or by vehicle, sort and scan by address and sequence, handle mail requiring a signature, and hand over undelivered and exception items.
